q: Which allowances on my payslip are tax free, and up to how much?
answer:
I've read the tax-free allowances pages, so here's the answer.

## Tax-free allowances and their caps

| Allowance | Tax-free cap | Condition |
|---|---|---|
| Meals | 200,000 KRW a month | Only if meals in kind (e.g. a canteen) aren't also provided |
| Own-car use | 200,000 KRW a month | Your own vehicle, used for work. Not alongside a per-kilometre claim for the same vehicle |
| Childcare | 200,000 KRW a month | Child aged 6 or under. It stops automatically in the year they turn 7 |
| Research | 200,000 KRW a month | Qualifying roles only |
| Trip daily allowance | "Reasonable actual cost" | Within policy rates: 20,000 KRW a day domestic, USD 50–80 a day overseas |

## How the caps behave
- **Over a cap:** only the excess is taxed. A 250,000 KRW meal allowance against the 200,000 KRW cap taxes 50,000 KRW.
- **Failing a condition:** the whole line becomes taxable, not just part of it. An example is drawing the meal allowance while also using the canteen.
- **Trip allowance:** it is taxed in two cases.
  - **Unconfirmed day:** an allowance for a day that attendance hasn't confirmed is treated as ordinary pay and is fully taxable.
  - **Double claim:** if you also claim a meal receipt as an expense on a day you drew the allowance, that amount moves back into taxable pay.

## On your payslip
The payslip lines page lists only the meal allowance (200,000 KRW) and own-car allowance (200,000 KRW) as fixed tax-free lines. The trip allowance appears as its own line, paid for days attendance confirms. Childcare and research allowances would show up only if you qualify.

I can't see your actual payslip. If a line looks taxed, check its condition above first. The two usual causes are an unconfirmed attendance day and a meal receipt claimed on an allowance day.

The two pages differ slightly on how a failed condition is treated. The payslip lines page only mentions "excess over cap is taxed". The tax-free allowances page adds that failing a condition makes the whole line taxable. I went with the tax-free allowances page because it is the more detailed one.
